workingTitle: A radio map resolves nearly 63,000 cosmic sources in one patch of sky
publicationStatus: Unreviewed preprint, accepted by Astronomy & Astrophysics
coreFacts: LOFAR observed ELAIS-N1 for 200 hours at 115-168 MHz over 2.5 by 2.5 square degrees.
Combining new sub-arcsecond imaging with earlier 6-arcsecond data yielded 62,916 unique radio sources.
Central sensitivity 5.3 microJy/beam at 0.33 by 0.39 arcseconds; positional alignment used 95 Gaia quasars.
The study demonstrates deeper low-frequency imaging, not a claim that all 62,916 objects were newly discovered.
